Master.The.Move.Anaconda.by.John.Danaher.overview: John Danaher's anaconda strangle study, eight volumes. Volume 1 covers the front headlock as the precursor. Volume 2 covers building an unstoppable anaconda and its most important position. Volume 3 covers the two-step method with the Olympic roll and the standard inside roll-through. Volume 4 covers takedown defence into the anaconda (the down block). Volume 5 covers guard passing into the anaconda and against seated opponents. Volume 6 covers the anaconda from side control and mount. Volume 7 covers the anaconda from the back (reverse kata gatame) and combining it with other submissions. Volume 8 covers what to do when you can't break the opponent down (front headlock Olympic roll strangle).
Master.The.Move.Anaconda.by.John.Danaher.for: No-gi grapplers who want a front headlock finish that works from many positions.
key: Anaconda from passing, pins and the back

Mikey Musumeci/Leg Pummeling Mastery by.overview: Mikey Musumeci on leg pummelling (fighting for inside position with your legs) as a way to pass, take the back and enter leg locks, six parts. Part 1 introduces the idea. Part 2 covers the leg drag with double leg control. Parts 3 and 4 cover inside sankaku (the 'honey hole') set-ups from double leg control and when the opponent grabs your leg, and closing the knee to flank to the back. Part 5 covers back takes when they grab your front leg, and the shin wedge to pass. Part 6 covers changing sides and keeping control.
Mikey Musumeci/Leg Pummeling Mastery by.for: No-gi players who play with leg entanglements on top or bottom.
key: Leg drag with double leg control

Mikey Musumeci/No-gi Berimbolo System Pa.overview: Mikey Musumeci adapts his gi berimbolo to no-gi, eight parts. Part 1 covers how control differs between gi and no-gi. Part 2 covers how to invert, with drills. Part 3 covers the basic berimbolo (one arm posted, legs-only drill). Part 4 covers alternative hip control and the supine berimbolo. Part 5 covers the 'top bolo' (including to the anaconda). Part 6 covers double frontal control (the 'ladderbolo', double leg bolo). Part 7 covers alternative leg drag set-ups (leg drag stack to twister hook). Part 8 covers partial frontal control into the twister hook and more.
Mikey Musumeci/No-gi Berimbolo System Pa.for: Flexible no-gi open guard players who want to invert to the back.

Mikey Musumeci/The Mikey Lock by Mikey M.overview: Mikey Musumeci's signature 'Mikey lock' leg lock, four parts. Part 1 introduces the lock and how to enter it. Part 2 covers the front foot finish and the front-side variations. Part 3 covers entries (from the K guard and others). Part 4 covers entries from the knee shield.
Mikey Musumeci/The Mikey Lock by Mikey M.for: No-gi leg lockers looking for a less common finish.
key: Entries from K guard and knee shield
